_date: DERIVED — Sunday 7 March 2027. Two days past collection, so a bin at the curb has been there a while.
_teaching: Clutter arrives (R-107) and the bins have LINGERED — Sunday is four days past the window, and one address has had them out since Wednesday. Also the first person bounty: a face on a notice you have to recognise in the street.
briefing: Sunday. Article XII is live from today — accumulated junk and debris. Containers have been at the curb on one of these since Wednesday, which the file will show you.
_cameos: CJ and Liz with Chaz, on the shift after the one where he was missing. Finding the cat on Shift 2 and then meeting the couple he belongs to is the payoff for having read the notice.
story: Sunday round. Nobody expects you on a Sunday, which is presumably why the board schedules one.
Article XII joins the list today: clutter. Neatly stacked material for a live project is not an accumulation. A sofa is.

artifact.title: Clipped to the binder
artifact.text: A board review memo. “Your predecessor’s accuracy was 94%. We mention it as a benchmark.”

bounty.headline: Wanted

bounty._placement: The character is DRAWN AT RANDOM per level, not authored — the player is meant to recognise a face off a notice, and a fixed face gets memorised instead. Whichever lot is chosen always has a resident out, and it is always them.

lots._teaching: Clutter introduced on a lot with nothing else wrong, so the new article is met on its own.

violations.why: Upholstered furniture accumulated on the front lawn.

lots._teaching: The lingering bins. Out since Wednesday, four days past the window — the first_seen date on the object is the evidence.

violations.why: At the curb since 3 March. Four days past the window.

lots._teaching: The clutter decoy: boxes stacked neatly for an active project are not an accumulation. On the driveway rather than the lawn, which is where a live project actually stages — and the fence beside them is sound.

decoys.why: Neatly stacked in support of an active project — R-107 covers accumulation, not storage.

lots._teaching: Weeds and a washer. Two live articles on one lot, both real — and the washer is on the driveway, so the article is not learned as 'junk on grass'.

violations.why: A discarded appliance on the driveway.
Unbordered weed growth in the front turf.

lots._teaching: Clean close. Screened bins on a non-collection day, which by now should be automatic.
